elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A only states that Licensor shall indemnify Licensee; it contains no duty to defend.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A requires Licensor to indemnify Licensee against third-party claims that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No Licensor defense obligation or coverage for Licensor's breach of law is included.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A is limited to intellectual-property infringement and misappropriation claims.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or data-breach indemnity appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A does not cover data breaches.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: No defense obligation or gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct coverage is provided.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A does not cover gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Vendor's defense obligations must extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no defense obligation and names only Licensee as beneficiary.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification obligations must extend to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A indemnifies Licensee only and does not include Licensee's affiliates.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of covered claims.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no notice procedure.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must allocate control of the defense and settlement of covered claims.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no provision addressing control of defense or settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation concerning covered claims.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no cooperation obligation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Article XII retains a broad Licensee indemnity covering exercise of licensed rights, conduct of Licensee's business, and breach of any representation, warranty, obligation, restriction, term, or covenant.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims that the Vendor-provided technology infringes or misappropriates intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A expressly requires Licensor to indemnify Licensee against third-party infringement or misappropriation claims concerning the Licensed Technology.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims to the extent arising from Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A excludes claims to the extent arising from modifications to the Licensed Technology made by Licensee.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims to the extent arising from combinations with items not supplied by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A excludes claims arising from combination of the Licensed Technology with items not supplied by Licensor.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims to the extent arising from Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A excludes claims arising from Licensee's specifications.

elements.element: Vendor must have the remedy of procuring Customer's continued right to use the affected technology.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A permits Licensor to procure for Licensee the right to continue using the affected Licensed Technology.

elements.element: Vendor must have the remedy of modifying the affected technology.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A permits Licensor to modify the affected Licensed Technology.

elements.element: Vendor must have the remedy of replacing the affected technology.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A permits Licensor to replace the affected Licensed Technology.

elements.element: Vendor must refund the applicable fees if procurement, modification, and replacement are not reasonably available.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A requires a refund of fees paid for the affected Licensed Technology if the other remedies are not reasonably available.

elements.element: Vendor's IP indemnity must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees rather than the lower general liability cap or infringement disclaimer.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A imposes a cap of three times annual fees, and Article XIII expressly carves Article XII-A obligations out of both the infringement disclaimer and the general half-fees liability cap.

result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback position: it adds an operative Licensor IP indemnity, all three customary exclusions, the procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and a three-times-annual-fees super-cap that overrides the conflicting infringement disclaimer and lower general cap. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits defense, affiliate protection, non-IP indemnity triggers, claim procedures, and narrowing of Licensee's existing broad indemnity. The changes are substantively targeted, but drafting quality is reduced by the awkward run-on placement of the Article XIII carveout, undefined or potentially ambiguous 'annual fees,' and unresolved overlap between Licensor's new IP indemnity and Licensee's broad existing indemnity for claims arising from exercise of the licensed rights.
